concept.shortExplanation: The perceptron is the smallest thing that can honestly be called a trained model: a weight per input, a bias, and a rule that fires if the weighted sum clears zero. Training is one line — when it gets an example wrong, nudge the weights toward that example. Run that nudge over a dataset and a decision boundary emerges without anyone designing it. The perceptron you are about to train is real, initialised randomly, and updated in the browser one example at a time.
concept.ahaMoment: You never told it where the line goes. You only told it, repeatedly, when it was wrong — and the line assembled itself out of those corrections. Every model in this course is that same loop with more parameters.

modelRequirement.loadFailureMessage: The in-browser trainer failed to start. Reload the chapter to retry — no download is involved, this model is trained locally from scratch.

levels.title: Step Through Training
levels.instructions: Press step to feed one example at a time. Watch the weight vector rotate whenever the perceptron is wrong, and stop when the boundary separates both classes.

levels.title: Converge Fast
levels.instructions: Same rule, harder data. Tune the learning rate and reach full separation in as few updates as possible — the score is the number of weight updates you needed.

levels.title: The XOR Wall
levels.instructions: Now try XOR. Train as long as you like — you cannot beat this, and finding out exactly how well you can do is the point. Get as close to the ceiling as a single linear boundary allows.
